record.paper_title: Open questions and perspectives for hadron electromagnetic form factors in space-like and time-like regions.
record.context_brief: Impact of revised nucleon form factors on light-nucleus descriptions
record.original_question: Given polarization measurements of elastic electron-proton scattering that show a large deviation of the ratio G_E/G_M from the older dipole-scaling expectation G_E(Q^2) = G_M(Q^2)/μ_p ≃ G_D, what are the consequences for descriptions of light nuclei, such as the deuteron or helium-3, that use nucleon electromagnetic form factors as inputs?

evidence.quote: They all suggest the following behavior: GE (Q2) = GM (Q2)/µp ≃ GD, GD(Q2) = (1 + Q2[GeV2]/0.71)−2.
The data, not only showed a very large precision, but also a large deviation of the ratio GE/GM from one, expected from Eq. (2).
• what are the consequences of these data for the light nuclei, like deuteron or 3He, which are often described with the help of nucleon FFs?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background and setup. For elastic electron–nucleon scattering, the nucleon electromagnetic structure is encoded in two form factors per nucleon: the Sachs electric form factor G_E(Q^2) and the Sachs magnetic form factor G_M(Q^2), where Q^2 is the negative of the squared four-momentum transfer. Historically, Rosenbluth-separation measurements on the proton suggested the dipole-scaling behavior

  G_E^p(Q^2) ≈ G_M^p(Q^2)/μ_p ≈ G_D(Q^2),   G_D(Q^2) = (1 + Q^2[GeV^2]/0.71)^{-2},

with μ_p the proton magnetic moment. Polarization-transfer measurements of elastic e–p scattering instead yield a ratio μ_p G_E^p(Q^2)/G_M^p(Q^2) that decreases significantly (approximately linearly) with increasing Q^2 over the few-GeV^2 range, in clear disagreement with the dipole-scaling assumption.

Light nuclei such as the deuteron (^2H) and helium-3 (^3He) are commonly described theoretically by combining a nuclear wave function (from a nucleon–nucleon interaction model, possibly supplemented by two- and three-body currents and relativistic corrections) with the single-nucleon electromagnetic form factors G_E^{p,n}(Q^2), G_M^{p,n}(Q^2) entering through the one-body electromagnetic current operator. Elastic electron scattering observables of these nuclei (e.g. the deuteron form factors A(Q^2), B(Q^2), and tensor polarization T_{20}(Q^2); the ^3He charge and magnetic form factors F_C(Q^2), F_M(Q^2)) thus depend explicitly on the nucleon form factors used as input.

Problem. Determine, quantitatively and qualitatively, the consequences for theoretical predictions of elastic electromagnetic observables of light nuclei — in particular the deuteron and ^3He — when the proton form factors used as nucleon-level inputs are taken consistent with the polarization-transfer behavior (μ_p G_E^p/G_M^p decreasing with Q^2) rather than with the older dipole-scaling assumption G_E^p ≈ G_M^p/μ_p ≈ G_D. Specifically:

(a) Identify and compute the modifications induced in the predicted deuteron observables A(Q^2), B(Q^2), and T_{20}(Q^2), and in the ^3He elastic charge and magnetic form factors F_C(Q^2) and F_M(Q^2), over the momentum-transfer range where the polarization data deviate appreciably from dipole scaling.

(b) Assess how such input changes affect the extraction of the neutron electromagnetic form factors G_E^n(Q^2) and G_M^n(Q^2) from quasi-elastic or elastic electron scattering on deuteron and ^3He targets, where nuclear corrections are required because no free-neutron target exists.

(c) Determine to what extent the resulting discrepancies (if any) between theory and data on light nuclei can be absorbed into meson-exchange currents, relativistic corrections, or modifications of nucleon structure in the nuclear medium, versus indicating genuine new physics in the nuclear electromagnetic current.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is an active research direction rather than a settled mathematical theorem. Reviews and analyses of nucleon form factors (e.g., dispersion-theoretical analyses and global fits) continue to refine the inputs used in deuteron and ^3He calculations, and extractions of the neutron form factors from ^2H and ^3He targets are still being updated. No single definitive answer fully quantifies the consequences across all observables, and the topic remains under continuing theoretical and experimental investigation.

status_evidence.title: Dispersion-theoretical analysis of the electromagnetic form factors of the nucleon: Past, present and future
status_evidence.snippet: Recent results from polarization methods have stimulated a revision of nucleon models and their use in nuclear calculations.
status_evidence.claim: The revision of nucleon form factors from polarization data is an ongoing program affecting nuclear-physics inputs.

status_evidence.title: Elastic Form Factors of the Proton, Neutron and Deuteron
status_evidence.snippet: Discussion of proton, neutron and deuteron elastic form factors with updated nucleon inputs.
status_evidence.claim: Light-nucleus form factor descriptions are continuously updated as nucleon form factor inputs are revised.

status_evidence.title: Relativistic rank-one separable kernel for helium-3 charge form factor
status_evidence.snippet: Recent helium-3 charge form factor calculations in the relativistic impulse approximation use updated nucleon form factors.
status_evidence.claim: ^3He elastic form factor predictions continue to be reanalyzed using revised nucleon form factors.
